pages.text: $(l)Build a Tinkers' Smeltery right away.$() It doubles ores, makes alloys and makes steel. It doesn't need to be big.$(li)Alloys: 1 copper + 1 nickel = 2 Constantan. Aluminum Brass = copper + aluminum (not to be confused with Brass = copper + zinc).
$(li)Automation: a chest and pipe feed the input, and a $(l)single active lever$() on the faucet pours continuously. No clock needed.

$(li)$(l)Thermal Expansion machines$() are the cheapest and easiest for basic Chapter 1 processing. Use EnderIO only when an alloy requires it, and skip NuclearCraft until you have a full Thermal set.

$(li)Thermal machines and dynamos need a $(l)Hardened upgrade kit$() before they accept augments.$(li)Grinders: Thermal Pulverizer, EnderIO SAG Mill, or a Cyclic Auto Clicker + Quartz Grindstone.$(li)Steel: roughly 1.05–1.1 coal coke per iron in the blast furnace.

$(l)Treated Wood:$()$(li)Loot the $(l)Immersive Engineering village house$() (treated wood and green wool). Its IE crates keep their contents when broken.$(li)Later, a Redstone Furnace with the Pyrolytic Conversion augment is the best method.
$(li)The IE Coke Oven works but is very slow.$(li)In a Sequential Fabricator, add a $(l)Pattern Validation$() augment. Otherwise it fills up with wood, forgets the creosote, and stalls.
